key_insight: Laser breakdown inside micrometer water droplets creates an internal pressure load that drives either thin-film collapse at low energy or explosive liquid-shell expansion and atomization at high energy, while ambient pressure mainly changes the emitted shock wave rather than the droplet motion.
engineering_relevance: These results help predict laser–droplet interactions in spray processing, diagnostics, and microexplosion-based atomization where coupled liquid deformation and shock emission matter.
method: Nanosecond laser-induced breakdown experiments on micrometer water droplets in the finite-beam regime (D0/Db ~ 2).
Simultaneous measurement of liquid deformation and emitted shock waves over a range of ambient pressures.
Comparison of low-energy and high-energy regimes to separate shell dynamics from gas-phase blast propagation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experimental observations showing distinct shock-wave and droplet-expansion behaviors across laser energy regimes and ambient pressures, with shock dynamics matching strong blast wave theory.
watch_item: The findings are specific to the tested droplet size, finite-beam focusing conditions, and laser-energy range, so extrapolation to other geometries or fluids should be done cautiously.
paper_title: Ambient-pressure effects on shock emission and liquid-shell expansion following optical breakdown inside water droplets
